articles.summary: Earnings-call recap: Millrose guides Q4 AFFO to $0.82-$0.84 a share, says leverage ended Q3 at 36% against a 33% target after its roughly $1.1B Dream Finders commitment, and that 42% of assets now sit outside the Lennar program.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is above its own leverage target after the Dream Finders deal, which limits how hard it can bid for new builder programs until takedowns repay debt.

articles.summary: Millrose Q3: AFFO $0.80 a share, invested capital about $9.25B. Lennar book yields 8.5%; other builders 10.8%. Closed about $1.1B for Dream Finders' Beazer purchase: $580M land bank on 7,000 homesites plus $488M of 12% preferred. $250M buyback authorized.
articles.why_it_matters: Millrose is pricing non-Lennar option capital at 10.8% and is now writing preferred equity alongside land banking to win a builder's M&A financing, a package Domain will be asked to match.

suggested_update.text: Millrose provided about $1.1B tied to the Beazer acquisition (closed 2026-10-20): about $580M of land banking across roughly 7,000 homesites plus about $488M of 12% preferred equity.

articles.summary: Kennedy Lewis is taking a majority stake in roadsurfer, a Munich-based camper-van rental company.
articles.why_it_matters: No bearing on Domain beyond showing Millrose's manager deploying capital outside housing.

articles.summary: Century Communities' board on Nov. 4, 2026 elected James Francescon, 37, President effective Jan. 1, 2027. His father Robert Francescon stays CEO and becomes sole principal executive officer; Dale Francescon is Executive Chairman.
articles.why_it_matters: The next-generation leader at a top-10 builder is now named, and he comes from private equity and investment banking, so he is a person Domain should get in front of on land-capital decisions.

suggested_update.text: James Francescon (EVP, Corporate Operations) becomes President effective 2027-01-01; Robert J. Francescon remains CEO and becomes sole principal executive officer (8-K filed 2026-11-09).

articles.summary: Lennar on Oct. 26, 2026 restated its unsecured revolver: commitments rise to $3.795B with a $750M accordion, and the main tranche extends to November 2031. It also drew $40M more term loan, to $1.75B due May 2028.
articles.why_it_matters: Lennar has locked in more and longer bank liquidity at slightly lower cost, which sets the bank-debt benchmark Domain's land-bank pricing to Lennar is measured against.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility amended and restated 2026-10-26: commitments $3.795B plus $750M accordion, Class A maturity November 2031; term loan increased to $1.75B, due May 2028.

articles.summary: D.R. Horton added Carl E. Reichardt Jr., a retired BTIG partner, as an independent director effective Oct. 22, 2026, expanding the board to nine. No officer change.
articles.why_it_matters: A board addition, not a change in who runs land or finance at D.R. Horton, so nothing for Domain to act on.

articles.summary: Ocean Aviation, backed by Kennedy Lewis, broke ground on a private aviation campus at Miami Executive Airport.
articles.why_it_matters: Unrelated to builder land; a Kennedy Lewis portfolio company in aviation real estate.

articles.summary: Millrose announced the date of its third-quarter 2026 earnings release and conference call. The results have since been published (Oct. 27).
articles.why_it_matters: A scheduling notice already overtaken by Millrose's actual Q3 results, so it tells Domain nothing new about the competitor.

articles.drop: Reference/profile page about TPG Angelo Gordon, not a news story or event.

articles.summary: Green Brick Partners appointed Jed Dolson, identified in the filing as Co-Chief Executive Officer, to its board effective Oct. 22, 2026, expanding the board to seven. No officer departed.
articles.why_it_matters: A board seat for an existing Green Brick leader; it does not change who Domain would call on land or finance.

articles.summary: Lennar shares fell on Oct. 2, 2026 after Hunterbrook, which is short Lennar and Millrose, alleged Lennar met quarterly targets by selling hundreds of completed homes to Millrose late in the quarter. The claims are unproven.
articles.why_it_matters: Public scrutiny of how arm's-length the Lennar-Millrose relationship is gives Lennar a reason to spread land-bank business to other providers, Domain included.

articles.summary: Century Communities amended its credit agreement on Sept. 30, 2026: commitments rise to $1.2B and maturity extends to Nov. 1, 2030 for extending lenders. Flagstar and Morgan Stanley join; BMO does not extend. U.S. Bank is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: Century has a larger, longer bank revolver to fund land on balance sheet, which reduces its near-term need for land-bank capital.

suggested_update.text: Credit agreement amended 2026-09-30: aggregate commitments increased to $1.2B and maturity extended to 2030-11-01 for extending lenders.

articles.summary: Starwood Capital and Canada's Trez Capital formed a residential land financing venture with a planned $450M seed round, targeting more than $1B of originations a year for single-family land and development.
articles.why_it_matters: A large institutional name is putting a billion dollars a year into residential land lending, new capital competing for the same builder and developer land deals Domain finances.

articles.summary: Strata Land Partners launched Nov. 2, 2026, backed by Wafra and Hunt Companies and led by Michael Forsum, former Landsea Homes president. Its first projects cover about 1,300 lots; capital committed was not disclosed.
articles.why_it_matters: A new land-capital platform aimed at public and especially private builders nationwide, run by an operator who knows builders personally, is a direct new competitor for Domain's mid-size builder deals.

articles.summary: Investor analysis from September: Millrose's non-Lennar capital earned 10.6% against 8.5% on the legacy Lennar portfolio as of June, with shares near 0.87 times book. Since superseded by Q3 figures.
articles.why_it_matters: Shows the roughly two-point premium Millrose charges builders other than Lennar, a reference point for Domain's own option pricing.

articles.summary: LGI Homes amended its revolver on Oct. 9, 2026: commitments total about $1.166B including a $175M incremental facility, with $855M extended to Oct. 9, 2030. Borrowing-base values and covenants were modified; details not disclosed. Wells Fargo is agent.
articles.why_it_matters: LGI owns most of its land and funds it on this revolver, so a borrowing-base and covenant reset is a moment to ask whether it wants off-balance-sheet lot capital.

suggested_update.text: Revolver amended 2026-10-09: commitments about $1.166B including a $175M incremental facility; $855M (73.3%) now matures 2030-10-09.

articles.summary: Dream Finders Homes exercised a committed accordion on Oct. 9, 2026, raising its revolving credit commitments by $220M to about $1.7B. Other terms unchanged.
articles.why_it_matters: Dream Finders was stacking bank capacity days before closing Beazer, alongside Millrose's land bank and preferred, showing how much outside capital this customer now needs.

suggested_update.text: Revolving credit facility commitments increased by $220M to about $1.7B via accordion exercise on 2026-10-09.

articles.summary: Beazer signed supplemental indentures on Sept. 18, 2026 after a Dream Finders consent solicitation, amending the change-of-control definition in its 8.000% notes due 2032 and 7.500% notes due 2031 so the merger would not trigger it.
articles.why_it_matters: Beazer's notes stay outstanding inside Dream Finders rather than being refinanced, so the combined builder carries more debt and has more reason to keep land off balance sheet.

articles.summary: Dream Finders sold $225M of 12% Series B convertible preferred on Sept. 14, 2026, with 450,000 more shares due at the Beazer merger closing. Proceeds redeem about $154.3M of Series A. Millrose says it bought about $488M of the preferred.
articles.why_it_matters: A top-15 builder paid 12% for preferred equity to fund an acquisition and a land banker supplied most of it, a sign of what builders will pay and what competitors will offer beyond lot options.

suggested_update.text: Issued $225M of 12% Series B convertible preferred on 2026-09-14, with a further 450,000 shares ($1,000 liquidation preference each) committed for the Beazer merger closing; Series A preferred redeemed for about $154.3M.

articles.summary: Avila Real Estate Capital raised $390M from an insurer and a university endowment, taking total capital above $750M. It lends against land, lots and homes for builders; investors include D.R. Horton, LGI, Century, Toll, Dream Finders and DRB.
articles.why_it_matters: A builder-backed lot lender with a stated goal of financing 100,000 lots in five years is competing capital for the finished-lot deals Domain funds, and six top-20 builders are its investors.
